# The tests protect how a FAT or exFAT stick is identified on Linux and macOS, which no earlier test reached:
# volume IDs per file system on both systems (the serial with the file system and size, Disk Arbitration on
# macOS 15, udev records for exFAT on Linux), a record made before sizes were in the ID that the first scan
# back replaces, and sticks with one serial of the same and of different sizes, swapped live and while
# stopped. Most cases started as a reviewer's failing probe. Cases that share setup already run as tables
# over FAT, exFAT, live and stopped; the rest differ in their order of mounts, ejects and restarts, so
# merging them further drops a case. Fixture guards detach loop devices and mounts when a test fails, and
# the review cases cover a rescan of one file across a stick change, ext4 roots born on one side, two sticks
# with one serial mounted at once, and an ignored mount point that cannot be opened. rustfmt's wrapping of the ejected_volumes fragment adds 54.
